chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Excess of sleep is a cause of ruin for religion and the world.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world — one's worldly life, livelihood, and social responsibilities
key_terms.الدِّين: Religion — one's religious practice, obligations, and spiritual state
key_terms.كَثْرَةُ النَّوْمِ: Excess of sleep — not sleep itself, but its excess, indicating a measured criticism of laziness
key_terms.مَذْهَبَةٌ: A thing that causes departure or ruin; derived from dhahaba (to go away), indicating both loss and destruction

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about excessive sleep in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns that excessive sleep destroys both one's religious commitment and worldly affairs. This terse aphorism reflects the Islamic emphasis on productive use of time as a religious duty — the original audience of early Shia companions would have understood 'religion' as one's ritual obligations and spiritual state, and 'world' as one's livelihood, responsibilities, and social duties. The hadith comes with a weak link in the chain (an anonymous narrator), reflecting the practical reality of early transmission.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Frequency of the sleeping (lead to) departure of the Religion and the world’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from the one whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’
Excessive sleeping causes one to lose his religion as well as the worldly matters.”’
